plotSections.title: Morning split
bullets: It is morning. The party spent the morning working out where people had been, including a possibility that Barker made a deal with Vecna and something about a sister-skin journal.
They leave the forest in two groups. Walker and Ciri head for Carlkin's lighthouse with Ord, Dana, Elrus, and Araden. Sylan and Gerk stay to deal with spirits.
Ord and Ciri need a ride to fly. Dana's broom cannot take a passenger. Araden carries one of them and, tapping their chest, says their wings are in there.

plotSections.title: The gray field and the raven
bullets: Sylan enters the sword. He turns translucent, so Gerk's rocks fall through him and pile at his feet. The gray field is emptier than before. Sylan confirms the giant once held there was released and that no one is in there now. Distant figures are still visible.

Sylan prays and tries to draw six spirits to him. Arcana 21. The grass at his feet darkens and he feels a fishing-line pull toward them. Before they arrive, a raven drops to within a few feet, studies him, and becomes a feather-draped person between a halfling and a dwarf.

The emissary calls him Razor, says the spirits were not attached, that he already sent them on, and asks why he is pulling them back. Sylan lets the pull go. The emissary says he is Raven's razor and the pathway to the falls, and that a razor of the Raven Queen must seek out those who—then the line is lost when the mic cuts out. Sylan thanks them and stops the summoning. The spirits had said they still had things left; he answers that it is time they moved on. The emissary begins, "They did, but she will say," and does not finish. Sylan leaves the figure in the gray field and returns to the rock pile.

plotSections.title: New Navel and Shades and Trades
bullets: Sylan tells Gerk the sword-state is not something he wants to share, though Gerk could come sometime. He drops the ghost-cop sweep. He thinks walking through New Navel last time made spirits follow him, and that spirits are still walking the town.

His duty is to gather souls and move them on, including hunting ones who cling out of jealousy or greed. He does not want to force anyone, and he is not sure what to do about spirits who are not those "bad ones."

Gerk will find the mayor or the sheriff and ask for word to go out: spirits who want to move on should find Sylan. If the mayor is a spirit, Gerk will do the talking. Sylan will avoid the spirits for now, wait outside town if needed, and go to Shades and Trades, which sits in the middle of town. He believes the person there was alive, not a spirit. Gerk can meet him after the ask.

chronologicalEvents: Morning: the party finishes comparing where people have been. Barker may have dealt with Vecna, and a sister-skin journal is noted as concerning.
Walker and Ciri's group leaves the forest for Carlkin's lighthouse. Elrus goes with Araden. Sylan and Gerk stay.
Gerk tries to stack rocks on Sylan as Sylan enters the sword. Sylan is translucent, so the rocks fall through and Gerk outlines his feet instead.

Inside the sword, the gray field is mostly empty. Sylan confirms he released the giant and is holding no one. He sees distant figures and, after a prayer and an Arcana check of 21, starts reeling six spirits toward him.
A raven confronts him, becomes a feather-draped halfling-or-dwarf figure, and questions why Razor is pulling spirits he already sent on. Sylan releases them.
The emissary names him Raven's razor and the pathway to the falls, starts to define whom he must seek, and is cut off. Sylan agrees not to pull more back and leaves.

Back outside, Sylan sends Gerk to the mayor or sheriff of New Navel to ask which spirits would willingly move on, and heads for Shades and Trades while trying not to pick up spirits in town. He is still unsure how to treat spirits who are not clinging out of greed.

Sylan.existing: Half-elf rogue and Gilbrick Gatekeeper with a cautious bond to the Raven Queen; his sword opens a gray spirit field.
notes: Confirms the giant previously held in the sword was released and that the field is empty except for distant figures.
Arcana 21 lets him pull on six spirits he is concentrating on. He stops when told they were not attached and that he had already sent them on.
Told he is Raven's razor and the pathway to the falls, and that it is his duty to seek out those who—the rest is lost to a mic cut.
He believes passing through New Navel caused spirits to follow him. Many do not want to move on. He will not force them and wants to avoid town until he knows who is willing.
He plans to wait outside New Navel if needed, then go to Shades and Trades, and may return for spirits who choose to move on.
He offers that Gerk could enter the spirit field with him sometime, and says he does not intend for that to be soon.
personality: Does not want to force spirits who are not ready, even though he believes it is time for them to move on.
Treats the sword's gray field as private and unpleasant to share.
quotesThemes: "They tried to tell me they had things left, but it is time for them to move on."
He separates "bad ones" who cling from jealousy or greed from other spirits, and says he still has to reconcile what to do about the rest.
openQuestions: Whom must he seek? The emissary stopped at "those who" when the mic cut out.
What should he do about spirits who are not the ones clinging out of jealousy or greed? He says he is still trying to reconcile that, and the conversation breaks off on "What if they're."

notes: Stays with Sylan while the others fly toward Carlkin's. He can see Sylan turn foggy inside the sword, and the rocks he stacks fall through that form.
Sylan asks him to find the mayor or sheriff of New Navel and put out word for spirits who are willing to move on to come find Sylan.
If the mayor is a spirit, Gerk is the one who should do the talking. After that he can meet Sylan, who may be waiting outside town before Shades and Trades.
He asks what happens to the good spirits, as opposed to the ones who refuse to move on.
personality: Practical about the spirit problem: he asks who is supposed to go, what if the mayor is a spirit, and what about the good ones.
quotesThemes: "So ask the mayor if he will put out an announcement that any spirits looking to go to their afterlife should find you."

Raven emissary.existing: An unnamed raven who becomes a feather-draped person and calls Sylan Raven's razor.
notes: Appears in the sword's gray field when Sylan starts pulling the six spirits: a raven within two or three feet, then a feather-draped, middle-aged person who could be a slight dwarf or a heavily built halfling.
Says the spirits were not attached to Sylan, that Razor already sent them on, and asks why he is pulling them back.
Calls him Raven's razor and the pathway to the falls. Says a razor of the Raven Queen must seek out those who—and does not finish.
After Sylan says the spirits claimed they had things left but should move on, answers "They did, but she will say," and does not finish. Sylan leaves them in the gray field.
personality: Speaks to Sylan as someone already under orders, and checks that he is not still pulling the spirits back.
quotesThemes: "No, they were not attached to you. Razor, you have sent them on their way. Why do you pull them back?"
"You are Raven's razor. You are the pathway to the falls."
"You are a razor of the Raven Queen. It is your duty to seek out those who."
openQuestions: The emissary does not finish who Sylan is supposed to seek, or what "she will say."

Raven Queen.existing: Elder god of death, also called Nira.
notes: Through the emissary, Sylan is named a razor of the Raven Queen, with a duty to seek certain souls.
The emissary starts to defer to her—"she will say"—and does not finish the sentence.

Sylan's sword.existing: Opens a gray spirit field where Sylan turns ghostly and can pull spirits toward himself.
notes: Entering it is a semi-familiar state. The world shrinks into a rolling gray field that is relatively empty compared with earlier visits.
Sylan's body becomes translucent; solid objects pass through him. He returns with only the rocks Gerk left around his feet.
The giant once held there is confirmed released. No one is currently inside. Distant figures can still be seen, and Sylan can pull on spirits from the field until he releases that tension.
The field is not the Abyssal Plane. The DM used "abyssal" only as a description and corrected it.

New Navel.existing: A familiar stop with Carlkin's lighthouse; spirits have been stirred here before.
notes: Sylan remembers spirits still walking the town and thinks his last pass through it picked some of them up.
He wants the mayor or the sheriff asked to announce that any spirit willing to move on should find him. He would rather stay outside town than walk through again.
Shades and Trades is in the middle of town.

Shades and Trades.existing: Where Sylan found the staff later fused to Ord's lantern.
notes: Sylan plans to go there after the spirit-realm check, but he may wait outside New Navel first so he does not gather more spirits.
He believes the person he is going to see there was a living person, not a spirit. Gerk can meet him there after talking to the mayor, as long as that does not mean forcing a spirit along.

Barker.existing: Uncertain name; someone who might have dealt with Vecna.
notes: The morning's catching-up includes that Barker might have made a deal with Vecna. The table leaves it as uncertain.
openQuestions: Did Barker make a deal with Vecna? The recap leaves it as "who knows."

notes: A giant had been held in Sylan's sword. Sylan confirms he released that giant. The gray field is empty of held spirits afterward.

Araden.existing: A magically capable companion brought secretly to The Reach.
notes: Goes with Elrus in the group flying toward Carlkin's lighthouse.
Carries a party member who cannot fly on their own and tells them, tapping their chest, that their wings are in there.
quotesThemes: "Don't worry, little one. I will carry you."

Dana's magic broom.existing: Dana's flying broom from the white dragon hoard.
notes: Dana does not think it can take a passenger. The DM recalls a weight limit, or a weight limit that changes speed.

misTranscriptions.notes: The two groups leave this forest for Carlkin's and the New Navel errand.
Morning recap of Barker's possible deal.
Raised beside the Barker–Vecna note. The Raskina is the tome made from Vecna's sister. Could instead be a separate journal.
Build of the feather-draped emissary, between halfling and dwarf.
Said while Sylan is reeling the spirits in.
What the DM said after realizing the mic had cut off the emissary's "seek out those who." The intended end of the sentence was not recovered.
Sylan sends Gerk to the mayor or sheriff there.
Sylan describing the last time he walked through town.
Sylan saying the shop is in the middle of town.
Araden, while offering to carry someone. The name is not otherwise used.
Ord, in the exchange about not having wings and needing a ride.
The emissary calls Sylan "the pathway to the falls." Everfalls is the known place the Raven Queen has seen him. It may instead be a title as spoken.

openQuestions: Whom is Sylan, as the Raven Queen's razor, supposed to seek? The emissary's sentence was cut off after "those who."
What did the emissary mean by "They did, but she will say"?
What should be done with spirits who are not clinging out of jealousy or greed? Gerk asks about the good ones, and Sylan says he is still reconciling it.
Did Barker make a deal with Vecna?

newTerms.name: pathway to the falls
notes: Epithet the raven emissary gives Sylan in the same breath as Raven's razor. It may refer to Everfalls.

newTerms.name: Unnamed giant
notes: A giant Sylan had held in the sword's gray field. He confirms in this chunk that he released it, and no one is held there now.
